mongodb-fundamentals-sr6-02.reason: source_problem + tell: moves the source to the Update Documents tutorial ('To replace the entire content of a document except for the _id field ...'; 'The replacement document can have different fields from the original document'). Also replaces 'keeps' (preserve-family words were 0T/8F). Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr6-02.statement: replaceOne() carries over an existing status field that its replacement document omits.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr6-02.explanation: replaceOne() replaces the whole document content except _id with the replacement. Old fields that the replacement omits, such as status, disappear.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr6-02.misconception: replaceOne() merges replacement fields into the existing document.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr7-11.reason: ambiguous: the limits page names { allowDiskUse: true } as the fix when a spillable stage hits the per-operation limit, so the old statement could be defended as True. The new card tests the scope of the limit ('applies to the combined memory of all memory-tracked stages of the operation'; 'separate from the 100 megabyte per-stage memory limit'). The explanation leaves out spilling so it does not give away sr7-10. (final: fixed)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr7-11.statement: In MongoDB 9.0, the server applies its new query memory limit to each memory-tracked aggregation stage separately.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr7-11.explanation: MongoDB 9.0 caps the combined memory of all memory-tracked stages in one operation, such as $group and $sort together, rather than giving each stage its own budget.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr7-11.misconception: The 9.0 per-operation memory limit is a separate budget for each memory-tracked stage.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr8-10.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation was circular, and 'preserves' wrongly suggested sharded foreign collections were always allowed. The $lookup page says: 'Starting in MongoDB 5.1, you can specify sharded collections in the from parameter'. Statement unchanged. (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr8-10.statement: In a sharded cluster, the $lookup stage accepts a sharded foreign collection.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr8-10.explanation: Since MongoDB 5.1 the from collection of $lookup can be sharded, so guides that call for an unsharded foreign collection describe older releases.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-07.reason: weak_card, rewritten instead of dropped because r12 would otherwise have only 7 cards (3T). Uses the verifier's replacement, checked against the page: 'The application can either recompute the value with every write that changes the computed value's source data, or as part of a periodic job' and 'In a low write environment, the computation can occur in conjunction with any update'. (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-07.statement: With the Computed pattern, an application can refresh the stored result on each write to the source data.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-07.explanation: Recomputing on every source write suits low-write workloads. When writes are frequent, a periodic job can refresh the stored value at set intervals instead.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-10.reason: weak_card (strawman, and the 'server does the application's job' template), rewritten to keep r12 at 9 cards with 4T/5F. Uses the verifier's replacement, checked against the page: 'The outlier pattern requires more complex logic to handle updates' and 'You need to handle updates for outlier documents differently than typical documents'. (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-10.statement: The Outlier pattern simplifies update logic for documents whose array exceeds the threshold.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-10.explanation: Outlier documents need their own update logic: the application checks a marker such as has_extras and writes overflow values to a separate collection.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr12-10.misconception: Moving overflow values out of the main document makes updates simpler.

source.title: Group Data with the Outlier Pattern

mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-11.reason: explanation_error: 'discards' suggested the data is lost. By default MongoDB writes rollback data to BSON files under <dbpath>/rollback (createRollbackDataFiles is enabled by default). Statement unchanged. (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-11.statement: A replica set's successful {w:1} acknowledgment protects the write from rollback after a primary failure.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-11.explanation: A {w:1} write can roll back if the primary steps down before any secondary replicates it. The rejoining member reverts the write and by default saves it to rollback BSON files.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-11.misconception: Successful primary acknowledgment makes a write immune to replica set failover rollback.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-12.reason: ambiguous: read as a tendency, the old statement could be defended as True. The new statement makes the guarantee explicit. The elections page says: 'a lower priority instance can be elected as primary for brief periods, even if a higher priority secondary is available. Replica set members continue to call elections until the highest priority member available becomes primary.' (final: fixed)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-12.statement: In a replica set, an available higher-priority secondary blocks a lower-priority member from winning an election.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-12.explanation: Priority is best effort: a lower-priority member can briefly become primary while a higher-priority secondary is available. Members keep calling elections until the highest-priority available member wins.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr15-12.misconception: Member priority guarantees that a lower-priority member cannot win while a higher-priority one is available.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-04.reason: tell: removes 'preserves' and 'order' (preserve-family words were 0T/8F, 'order' 1T/5F). It also shortens the r3 false average after sr3-03 was dropped. Fact and answer unchanged ('Documents may be reordered by mongod ...'). (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-04.statement: With ordered: false, mongod inserts insertMany() documents in their input array sequence.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-04.explanation: For ordered: false, mongod may reorder insert operations to improve performance, so the application has no input-order guarantee.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-04.misconception: Unordered insertion continues after errors while guaranteeing input order.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-08.reason: tell: removes 'preserves' and 'order', two false-leaning words. Fact and answer unchanged: cursor.sort says documents tied on the sort key may be returned in any order, and the sort is not stable. (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-08.statement: MongoDB breaks ties between equal cursor.sort() keys by insertion sequence.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-08.explanation: MongoDB leaves the order of documents tied on sort keys unspecified, so insertion sequence is no stable tie-breaker. Add a unique field such as _id to the sort.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr3-08.misconception: Equal sort keys retain insertion order.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr2-12.reason: tell (form): dropping sr2-08 left the r2 true average 5.8 characters above the false average. This shorter wording brings the gap to about 4.9 and keeps 'automatically' on a true card ('automatically' would otherwise lean false at 1T/2F). Fact and answer unchanged ('MongoDB creates a unique index on the _id field during the creation of a collection'). (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr2-12.statement: MongoDB automatically gives an ordinary unsharded collection a unique _id index.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr2-12.explanation: An ordinary unsharded collection receives its unique _id index at creation, enforcing uniqueness of its document identifiers.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr13-08.reason: tell (form): dropping sr13-02 and sr13-09 left the r13 true average 6.9 characters above the false average. This shorter wording brings the gap to about 4.4. Fact and answer unchanged (In-progress Transactions and Write Conflicts). (final: keep)
mongodb-fundamentals-sr13-08.statement: A replica set transaction can abort on a write conflict when an outside write changes its document.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr13-08.explanation: If an outside write changes a document during an in-progress transaction and the transaction later tries to modify it, MongoDB aborts the transaction with a write conflict.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-04.reason: fit: shortened to fit a 195 by 422 screen, same fact and answer
mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-04.statement: A primary can give multi-document queries linearizable guarantees with read concern "linearizable".
mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-04.explanation: MongoDB's linearizable guarantees apply to reads whose filters uniquely identify a single document. The concern does not extend that guarantee to a multi-document result.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-04.misconception: Selecting linearizable read concern extends its guarantee to queries returning multiple documents.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-10.reason: fit: shortened to fit a 195 by 422 screen, same fact and answer
mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-10.statement: Majority write acknowledgment means a replica set's acknowledging secondaries have applied the change.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-10.explanation: Majority acknowledgment follows recording the change in the required members' oplogs. Secondary application proceeds asynchronously and can still lag.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr14-10.misconception: Majority acknowledgment waits for secondary document changes to finish.

mongodb-fundamentals-sr16-10.reason: fit: shortened to fit a 195 by 422 screen, same fact and answer
mongodb-fundamentals-sr16-10.statement: mongos supports retryable updateOne() changing non-_id shard-key values with full-key equality.
mongodb-fundamentals-sr16-10.explanation: A shard-key value change uses mongos and full shard-key equality in the filter. A retryable write meets the operation requirement; a transaction is another permitted context.
